draft.title: Archaeology and stratigraphy
card: Archaeology is the study of the past through the objects and remains people left behind. Archaeologists dig up a site in a careful way called excavation.
They dig layer by layer and record what they find in each layer. Over time, soil, ash and rubbish build up and form layers, called strata.
In undisturbed ground, the deeper layers are usually older. Objects in a deep layer are usually older than objects in a layer above it.
Digging, floods and animal burrows can mix up layers. Archaeologists look for signs of this, because mixed layers make dating less reliable.
draft.remember: Dig layer by layer: in undisturbed ground, deeper usually means older.

a.q: An archaeologist finds a clay pot in a deep layer and a coin in a layer above it. The ground is undisturbed. What can she say?
opts: The pot is probably older than the coin
The coin is probably older than the pot
The pot and the coin are the same age
Neither can be dated by its layer
a.why: In undisturbed ground, deeper layers are usually older, so the pot is probably older than the coin. The coin is not older just because it is easier to reach: it lies higher, so it was probably buried later.
a.clue: Which layer was laid down first, the deep one or the top one?

b.q: Workers dug a pit through a site in Jordan years ago and refilled it. An archaeologist finds a modern bottle in a deep layer. What is the best explanation?
opts: The layers were disturbed, so the bottle fell in later
The bottle is the oldest object at the site
Deep layers are always the newest at a site
The bottle was made at the same time as the site
b.why: A pit that was dug and refilled mixes layers, so a modern bottle can end up deep down. The bottle is not the oldest object, because deeper means older only in undisturbed ground.
b.clue: Think about what the digging did to the layers.

a.best: The pot is probably older than the coin

b.best: The layers were disturbed, so the bottle fell in later

problems.detail: The distractor 'Deep layers are always the newest at a site' uses 'always', while the card says deeper layers are 'usually' older.

The right option stands out. It is the longest, it is the only one that gives a reason, and it repeats the card's word 'disturbed'. With the stem's pit and the clue, a student could pick it without understanding stratigraphy.
The why says 'deeper means older only in undisturbed ground'. The card says deeper layers are 'usually' older in undisturbed ground, so 'only' overstates the rule.
